region: Van Duzer Corridor · Willamette Valley, Oregon
about: Brianne Day founded Day Wines with the 2012 vintage after years spent working harvests in Burgundy, Argentina, Australia and New Zealand, then at The Eyrie Vineyards and Brooks in Oregon. She now works out of Day Camp in Dundee, a collaborative winery and tasting room shared with other small producers, and is known for natural, low-intervention wines: wild-yeast fermentations, little added, most wines unfined and unfiltered, from growers who farm organically or biodynamically.

Johan Vineyard is an 85-acre, Demeter-certified biodynamic estate south of McMinnville and west of Salem, in the Van Duzer Corridor. Pacific winds funnel through a gap in the Coast Range here, cooling a low-lying site on marine sedimentary soils and stretching the season, so its grapes are often among the last Pinot Noir picked. Day ferments about 40% of the fruit as whole clusters, which adds a savoury, stemmy lift, and the 2021 is bottled at 13.3% alcohol.

Critics have described dried rose, boysenberry, sour cherry and blood orange with sage and earthy notes, and a long finish; Expect cranberry, red cherry, tobacco and tea over a medium body and balanced acidity. Tannins and acidity are firm in youth, so decant it now or keep it into the mid-2030s, when the whole-cluster savour and fruit should be fully knit together.
facts: Johan Vineyard, 85 acres, marine sedimentary soils
